question: What is the primary goal of workplace ergonomics in nursing?

options.A: Accelerating the speed of patient documentation during shifts
options.B: Fitting the work environment to the physical needs of the nurse
options.C: Increasing the number of patients a nurse can admit daily
options.D: Reducing the financial cost of hospital medical equipment

explanation: Ergonomics focuses on adapting tools and workspaces to match human capabilities and limitations, preventing injury and fatigue. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why does neglecting ergonomic principles often lead to nurses leaving the profession early?

options.A: It causes chronic, cumulative trauma injuries that end careers
options.B: It lowers hospital accreditation scores during routine inspections
options.C: It creates constant friction between nursing staff and management
options.D: It prevents nurses from learning new electronic health systems

explanation: Uncorrected physical strain over years results in permanent musculoskeletal damage, forcing early retirement or career changes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: What happens to local blood flow during prolonged static muscle contraction?

options.A: Blood flow becomes restricted, causing rapid muscle fatigue
options.B: Blood vessels dilate to release excess metabolic heat
options.C: Blood circulation doubles to supply extra oxygen to tissues
options.D: Blood pressure drops instantly throughout the entire body

explanation: Holding a fixed posture compresses blood vessels, starving muscles of oxygen and building up waste products. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Bending forward repeatedly to use poorly positioned computer terminals primarily stresses which anatomical structures?

options.B: Long bones of the lower extremities and ankles
options.C: Valves within the deep venous system of the legs
options.D: Lumbar vertebrae and supporting back muscles

explanation: Forward flexion shifts the center of gravity and places immense mechanical load on the lower back structures. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which disorder is directly linked to chronic wrist compression and repetitive keying?
explanation: Repetitive hand movements and wrist flexion compress the median nerve inside the carpal tunnel, causing pain and numbness. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: A nurse who stands for long shifts on hard floors without supportive footwear is most at risk for developing what condition?
explanation: Inadequate foot support during prolonged standing places excessive strain on the plantar fascia ligament in the foot. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: Where should the top of a computer monitor be positioned relative to the user's eyes?

options.A: Directly above the top of the head
options.B: At or slightly below eye level
options.C: Level with the middle of the chest
options.D: Far below the level of the desk

explanation: Aligning the screen top with or below eye level encourages a neutral neck posture, preventing upward or downward strain. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the correct angle for a nurse's elbows while typing at an electronic health record terminal?
explanation: Keeping elbows bent at a right angle prevents shoulder elevation and reduces tension in the forearms and wrists. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: When transporting a heavy mobile medication cart down a hospital hallway, what is the safest technique?

options.A: Pulling the cart behind you while twisting your torso backward
options.B: Steering the entire heavy load using only one outstretched arm
options.C: Pushing the cart forward with both hands close to the body
options.D: Running quickly to maintain momentum across long corridors

explanation: Pushing allows better visibility, uses body weight effectively, and keeps the spine aligned compared to pulling or twisting. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why does poor wheel maintenance on mobile medical carts create a physical hazard for nursing staff?

options.A: It causes the electronic charting screen to flicker and lose patient data
options.B: It raises the overall height of the workstation beyond recommended eye levels
options.C: It eliminates the braking mechanism, causing the cart to roll away unpredictably
options.D: It increases rolling resistance, requiring dangerous levels of physical force to move

explanation: Stuck or stiff wheels force nurses to strain their backs and shoulders to overcome friction during transport. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What common condition results from staring at electronic health record displays for prolonged periods?
explanation: Prolonged screen viewing reduces blink rates and strains eye muscles, leading to dryness, headaches, and blurred vision. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: How does excessive screen glare impact the eyes of a nurse working at a nursing station?

options.A: It increases tear production to an uncomfortable and unsafe level
options.B: It completely stops the eye from blinking for long periods
options.C: It permanently damages the retina within a few hours of exposure
options.D: It forces eye muscles to work harder to focus, causing strain and fatigue

explanation: Glare washes out screen text, making visual acquisition difficult and accelerating muscular and visual exhaustion. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of taking brief micro-breaks during a busy nursing shift?

options.A: Lowering the total number of patients assigned to the ward
options.B: Doubling the speed of electronic health record documentation
options.C: Resetting muscle tension and restoring local blood circulation
options.D: Eliminating the need to take a full meal break during the day

explanation: Short pauses interrupt static muscle contractions, allowing fresh blood flow to clear metabolic waste and relieve tension. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: When is the most practical time for a clinical nurse to incorporate a brief ergonomic micro-break?

options.A: During an active cardiac arrest resuscitation procedure
options.B: While administering intravenous medication to an unstable patient
options.C: While waiting for an electronic charting system to load
options.D: During the middle of a sterile surgical wound dressing change

explanation: Utilizing natural workflow lulls ensures breaks happen without compromising patient safety or clinical duties. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which institutional action is essential for addressing workplace ergonomic hazards effectively?

options.A: Requiring nurses to purchase their own ergonomic computer accessories
options.B: Investing in adjustable furniture and safe patient-handling technology
options.C: Eliminating all electronic charting in favor of paper documentation
options.D: Increasing the length of shifts to reduce the total number of handovers

explanation: Organizational support requires providing proper physical infrastructure and tools to protect staff across all hospital units. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why are routine safety audits important within hospital departments like intensive care units?

options.A: They determine which nurses work the slowest during night shifts
options.B: They identify high-risk physical hazards before staff suffer permanent injuries
options.C: They replace the need for individual daily stretching routines
options.D: They calculate the exact financial bonuses for nursing unit managers

explanation: Proactive audits catch unsafe equipment or poor room layouts early, preventing chronic musculoskeletal injuries among staff. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)
